title: F232: every exemption names the instrument that audits its reason
description: Thirty module constants share the {subject: sentence} shape and the shape cannot tell an exemption from a help table, so the classification is the work - the same first-filter problem F231 paid off, and the NOT_A_GATE pattern is the answer this repository already owns. Derive the tables, require each to name its reason-checker or a reason it can have none, both directions checked. The user-visible argument is that four defects in two field reports were one shape: a claim in the product that nothing checks against reality.
desiredOutcome: Every exemption table in the tree either names the instrument that audits its reasons, or carries a checked reason why it cannot - and a table added later cannot opt out by being forgotten.
summary: F232 closed with the instrument rather than the argument: `exemption_audit_drift()` derives every module constant shaped `{subject: sentence}` and requires each to name the function that audits its reasons or a checked reason it can have none, both directions. Its first measurement overturned the claim that opened the phase - several tables already had reason-audits.

Both directions, so a table added later cannot opt out by being forgotten and a row cannot outlive its subject.
